summary: Owen Flanagan is a philosopher working in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Archbishop Stepinac High School, Fordham University, and Boston University, and became a Professor of Philosophy at Duke University around 1996.

P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri (1890–1978) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Bishop Heber College, the Institute of Advanced Study in Education, Saidapet, and the University of Madras, holding posts at Bishop Heber College, Rajah's College, and Annamalai University.
P. T. Narasimhachar (1905–1998) was an Indology scholar. He studied under Mysore Hiriyanna at Maharaja's College, Mysore, between 1923 and 1926.
Padma Subrahmanyam works in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at Stella Maris College, Ethiraj College for Women, and Annamalai University under research supervisor T. N. Ramachandran.

Padmanabh S. Jaini (1923–2021) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sukhlal Sanghvi. He served as a professor and later professor emeritus at the University of California, Berkeley.

Pahalawattage Don Premasiri works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Peradeniya, University of Cambridge, University of Canterbury, and University of Hawaiʻi, later serving as professor and Pali and Buddhist Studies department head at Peradeniya.

Palmira Brummett is a historian who earned degrees from the University of Chicago and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. She was a professor at the University of Tennessee (~1989–2011) and a visiting professor at Brown University (2011–2016).
Palmo Kyi is a Tibetologist who studied under Hanna Havnevik, Rinzin Thargyal, and supervisor Per Kværne.

Pamela D. Winfield works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She held a post at Temple University in 2001 and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Elon University (attested 2015–2017).
Pamela Gutman (1944–2015) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She pursued studies at the University of Vienna and the Australian National University.

Pandurang Vaman Kane (1880–1972) was an Indologist and historian. Educated at Wilson College and the University of Mumbai, he served as vice-chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1947–1949) and National Professor of Indology for the Government of India (~1959–1972).

Parimal G. Patil works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard University and the University of Chicago (~1993–2002), and was appointed Professor at Harvard University around 2004.

Parul Dave-Mukherji specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. She completed her DPhil at the University of Oxford (1988–1991) under Alexis Sanderson and became a professor of Visual Studies and Art History at Jawaharlal Nehru University.

Pasang Wangdu (1952–2024) was a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied under Luciano Petech and Ernst Steinkellner, and held a professorship at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences.

Pascale Haag specializes in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat and at Paris Nanterre University under Marie-Claire Gay, holding a post at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences around 2005.
Pascale Hugon works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. She has held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and its Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.
Pataraporn Sirikanchana is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania and held a professorship at Thammasat University.

Patrice Ladwig works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Münster, the University of Edinburgh, and EHESS, later holding posts at the University of Bristol and the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology.

Patricia Berger works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. She earned her Ph.D. from UC Berkeley, served as Curator of Chinese Art at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco, and joined the History of Art faculty at UC Berkeley in 1996.

Patricia Buckley Ebrey is a historian and sinologist educated at the University of Chicago and Columbia University. She held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and the University of Washington, where she was Professor Emerita of History (1997–2020).
